channel.name: Clover & Bruno Stories
channel.spine: Polite kitten Clover, usually with Mama Rosa and Papa Fin, meets Bruno — a 70-year-old retired grumpy dog who never says yes the first time, usually with Pip. 70% of episodes bring both families together.
channel.tagline: Every day starts with Clover. Every legend starts grumpy.

models.image_note: Muse Image throughout, via the muse-image CLI skill (Meta Model API). THREE tiers, and they must not be confused. (1) CHANNEL MASTERS at bible/characters/reference_sheets/ - 7 locked identity sheets, read-only, never edited by a stage; they lock WHO a character is. (2) EPISODE SHEETS at episodes/<EPID>/visual/references/characters/ - generated fresh at 04b every episode, only for the characters that episode uses, conditioned on the master for identity and carrying THIS episode's look, feel and wardrobe. (3) FRAME-0 STILLS at 04f2 - one per clip, conditioned on the EPISODE sheet, not on the master. Owner decision 2026-10-29.
models.video_note: i2v, native prose, native audio. The generation unit is the clip: one approved frame-0 still conditions exactly one generation.

cast.anchor_note: CAST-001 Clover and CAST-004 Bruno are the two anchors. CAST-002 Rosa, CAST-003 Fin and CAST-005 Pip are family anchors; CAST-006 Mimi and CAST-007 Tico are street-recurring.
cast.maximum_speaking_characters_note: 6 for long-form, 3 for a Short's covered section. From bible/EPISODE_SPEC.md; preferred 3-4 on long-form.
character_rules: DEFAULTS, not laws (owner decision 2026-10-29). Depart from any of these when the story is better for it, and declare the departure in the episode's cast snapshot at 03a-writer. An unremarked departure is a defect; a reasoned one is the point.
Clover usually appears with at least one parent, often both.
Pip is loyal to Bruno; whose side he takes in a given episode is a story choice, not a fixed two-stage move.
cast.signature_beat: Bruno's Never-Yes-First: first answer is No with attitude, second is a reluctant yes followed by helping. RETAINED as a hard rule (owner, 2026-10-29) - and it is CHARACTER, not a gag. He is 70, retired, experienced and arrogant enough to want to seem apart from it all; agreeing straight away would cost him the version of himself he presents. The refusal is therefore inevitable, but the EXCUSE should vary every episode (retirement, the back, not-my-business, a counter-complaint) - that variation is where a writer's room inside the rule lives. A Bruno who reaches for the identical excuse every time is written as a mechanism, not a character.
cast.tier_note: Rosa (CAST-002) is a MAIN character - Clover's mother, core household, present in most episodes. Mimi (CAST-006) is SUPPORTING - Street Recurring, appears only when a story needs her. They must stay behaviourally distinct (Rosa steady, Mimi spirals) and Mimi must never absorb Rosa's role.

reference_tiers.tier0_identity: bible/characters/identity/ - ONE BARE FIGURE per character. No wardrobe, neutral pose, plain backdrop, no panels or labels. Locks WHO the character is. The root; conditioned on nothing.
reference_tiers.tier1_episode_sheet: episodes/<EPID>/visual/references/characters/ - this episode's look and wardrobe, conditioned on Tier 0. Only the characters the episode uses.
reference_tiers.tier2_frame0_stills: episodes/<EPID>/renders/stills/ - one per clip, conditioned on the Tier-1 episode sheet.
reference_tiers.never_condition_on_a_sheet: A character SHEET is a composed page - panels, backdrop, captions, style. Conditioning on one delivers the page: a 2026-10-29 six-run test (in the source repo C:\pycode\clover_and_paws) reproduced the source sheet's text labels despite the prompt saying 'no text', and its rendering style overrode every restyle attempt. Bare figures only.
reference_tiers.fix_at_the_root: If a Tier-1 sheet is wrong, fix Tier 0 and regenerate. Never patch the derivative.
reference_tiers.promotion_rule: Episode sheets are never promoted into Tier 0 - they carry one episode's wardrobe. Promotion applies only to a NEW recurring character on its second episode, which then gets its own BARE identity master and card.
reference_tiers.upload_ceiling: Flow's uploader silently rejects large references (12MB/3840x2160 and 22MB/5504x3072 both failed; ~2MB JPEG at 2752x1536 works). Keep Tier-0 masters inside that budget or upload a downscaled JPEG proxy - never modify the master.
reference_tiers.download_integrity: muse-image CLI --download can return images the current prompt did NOT produce - it appears to take the most recent images in the PROJECT. Verified 2026-10-29: a Bruno run returned two Clover images and one unrelated two-shot, zero Bruno. Generate ONE character per run into its OWN folder, hash every download against all previous downloads, and look at the image before promoting it. Critical at 04f2, where a stale still would land in the wrong clip's slot and render without anyone noticing.

identity_masters.papa_finn: bible/characters/identity/papa_finn_identity.png  (v1 import, NOT yet regenerated photoreal - regenerate when a clover-and-paws episode first casts Fin)
identity_masters._missing: mimi (CAST-006), tico (CAST-007) - generate when an episode first needs them.
identity_masters._v2_note: Regenerated photoreal 2026-10-29 from the v1 imports, per owner decision to redesign from scratch while staying close to the existing designs. Each is ONE bare figure: no clothing, permanent identity accessory only, plain seamless backdrop, no panels or labels. The v1 imports are retained alongside as provenance.
identity_masters._accessories_kept_when_bare: Clover: green collar with gold tag, plus her four-leaf clover CHEST FUR MARKING. Bruno: bronze spectacle chain with round tortoiseshell glasses. Pip: red bandana. Rosa: none.
identity_masters._clover_motif_rule: The four-leaf clover appears TWICE over: as a darker fur marking on her chest (intrinsic, survives undressing, on the identity master) AND repeated as a print or embroidery on the chest of every garment she wears. Owner decision 2026-10-29. Either alone fails - a garment hides the marking, and a garment-only motif dies when she changes clothes. Together she is never without it, which keeps 'is the clover visible?' a valid binary QA check at draft resolution.

format.aspect_ratio_note: LOCKED 16:9 for every format (owner decision 2026-10-29, reverting the 2026-10-29 format-dependent experiment). The proven LTX-2.5 graph is fixed-aspect 16:9, so every still, clip and render is 16:9. A 9:16 Short is a post-production reframe of that same 16:9 footage, never its own still or clip batch - the frame-0 still and the clip it conditions must share an aspect, so a format-dependent aspect would force a full re-generation of every still. The graph's ResolutionSelector is fixed, never set per episode.

render.prompt_format_note: Owner-locked PromptRelay-style beat packet, adopted 2026-10-29 from the vidgen-codex-ltx sibling where a 20-second LTX-2.5 render of the beat form outperformed the regular-prose alternative. Every clip prompt is one 'GLOBAL:: Continue from the still. … Low motion.' line plus 'BEAT:: <frames> ::' lines totalling 481. The frame labels are a model-facing pacing convention, NOT the old ComfyUI-PromptRelay node. Enforced by LTXV-D001/D002; see pipeline/LTX_I2V_CONTRACT.md. clover-and-paws has no live episode past 04e, so nothing here needs re-drafting.
render.generation_unit_note: One approved frame-0 still conditions exactly one 20-second clip. Postprod concatenates clips and bridges them with controlled inserts and room tone; it does not cut within one.
render.clip_duration_note: Fixed 20s for every clip on every channel in this repo, owner decision 2026-10-29. The imported bible originally specified an 8-15s performance unit and was corrected on import, so nothing in this repo states a different figure. At 24 fps this lands on 481 frames (1 + 8*60), satisfying LTX-2.5's num_frames%8==1 rule. vidgen-dist takes SECONDS and derives the frame count itself — never hand-enter a frame count.
render.aspect_ratio_note: LOCKED 16:9, every format (owner decision 2026-10-29). The LTX-2.5 two-stage graph's ResolutionSelector is fixed; 9:16 Shorts are a post-production reframe of the same 16:9 render, never a separate still or clip batch. See format.aspect_ratio_note.
render.spoken_word_band_note: At this channel's 140 wpm a 20s clip carries ~31-34 quoted words if speech fills ~67-73% of the clip, leaving room for visible action, chore/prop business and a productive tail. DERIVED FROM WPM, NOT MEASURED on LTX-2.5 — re-derive from the first pilot batch, see research section 6 open question 2. Bruno's delivery is deliberately slower than Clover's, so his clips will sit at the low end of the band.
render.style_echo: Photorealistic anthropomorphic cozy family, bipedal upright human-like posture, fine realistic fur texture, soft natural light, warm golden cozy grade, clean uncluttered composition, high-end photographic finish
render.max_prompt_words_note: RUNAWAY TRIPWIRE, not a ceiling (retired 2026-10-29). LTX-2.5 has no vendor word limit and the Gemma encoder is built for long prompts; the old 200 figure was LTX-2-era sibling guidance. LTXV-D004 warns past 450 to catch a repeated room inventory or duration filler only. A dense three-hander normally runs 260-330 words and must not be trimmed to fit. See pipeline/LTX_I2V_CONTRACT.md §Length.
render.negative_prompt_note: Appended to pipeline/negative-prompt-base.txt at 04g, plus a 'second <Name>' term per cast member in the episode. Drawn from bible/VISUAL_STYLE_CONTRACT.md's own realism lock, which names the specific defects this channel drifts toward rather than a generic style label. This is the ONLY place suppression lives: the same terms in a positive prompt cause the artifact they name (LTXV-D010 rejects them).
render.look_and_feel: Photorealistic image of anthropomorphic {species} with fine realistic fur texture and clear, readable facial expressions. Soft natural lighting with a gentle, cozy color grade in warm golden or bright daylight tones, evoking a tender, inviting, picture-book mood. Clean, uncluttered composition with a high-end photographic finish.
render.look_and_feel_note: Owner-declared 2026-10-29, and it settles the photoreal-vs-stylized question in favour of PHOTOREAL. {species} is substituted per sheet ('cats' / 'dogs' / 'cats and dogs') because the cast is mixed - the owner's string said 'cats' but Bruno and Pip are dogs. Everything else is verbatim. This governs 04b episode sheets and every 04f2 frame-0 still conditioned on them. The CHANNEL MASTERS remain stylized 3D and are unaffected: under the three-tier model they are identity scaffolding only, never the on-screen look.
render.style_echo_note: 'bipedal upright human-like posture' added 2026-10-29 after frame-0 stills rendered quadruped real cats: a crouching cat is a pose a real cat holds, so the animal prior reasserted. It lives here, once, rather than as a repeated sentence in every still prompt.

youtube.description_line_required: AI-generated original stories. Not real footage. Photoreal anthropomorphic cat and dog family stories — Kitten Clover and Grumpy Dog Bruno.

hard_safety_floor: Never frame content as real footage or as real animals.
No real, identifiable people, brands or logos.

No peril in Arc A / D / E and all Clover-only and Bruno-only content — there the worst outcome is a setback, a mess, or a plan going wrong. Bounded, non-graphic jeopardy is allowed ONLY inside Arc B (Stand Tall) and Arc C (Rescue Dash) and ONLY under ADVENTURE_ARCS_LOCKED.md 'Compliance for Action': no graphic violence (push, block, stand tall — never a punch or blood); no weapons; antagonists are faceless, non-speaking, two to three at most, and leave rather than are beaten; every rescue resolves safely (the tree falls away, the cart is stopped, no character is actually hurt); Clover is never in danger alone; spy arcs stay comedic and daytime. Reconciled per owner decision 2026-10-29 (see bible/IMPORT_NOTE.md §5).
Every background character must be stated as an anthropomorphic animal — a bare 'neighbours/kids/adults' renders as photoreal humans.
